qualifying_findings.source_title: Call for participation: Demonstrate MCP-based AI agent security with open identity standards
qualifying_findings.summary: The OpenID Foundation AI Identity Management Community Group invited implementers to demonstrate interoperable security for MCP clients, gateways, and servers using open identity standards, including cross-enterprise agent identity and authorization questions.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: MCP governance guidance should treat identity, authorization, and cross-organization delegation as runtime architecture questions, not only tool configuration. Local ingest should connect this to agent identity, gateway policy, and audit expectations.
named_entities: Artificial Intelligence Identity Management Community Group
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep broad standards and MCP background upstream; retain the local practice implication for governed MCP identity and cross-enterprise authorization.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Loops, Harnesses, and 6,000 Engineers: What the World's Fair Confirmed - and What Ships Today
qualifying_findings.summary: TrueFoundry framed AI Engineer World's Fair 2026 around loops, verification, and harness engineering, arguing that long-running agent loops need budgets, step ceilings, stall safeguards, approval gates, per-step traces, and evaluation layers.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: This is directly relevant to local harness architecture: production agent loops need bounded execution, output-path verification, visible traces, and cost controls before teams expand autonomous work volume.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Do not create local product pages; use the source for local harness, progress, verification, and audit practice notes.

qualifying_findings.source_title: TBAC: Task-Based Access Control for the Agent Age
qualifying_findings.summary: TrueFoundry argued that agents strain identity-centric RBAC, ABAC, and ReBAC because each task may need a different permission slice, short-lived credentials, per-agent identities, quotas, and approval checkpoints.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Local governance pages should distinguish stable user or team entitlements from task-scoped agent permissions. Retrieval and tool calls should carry the originating user, task, and authorization decision instead of relying on broad standing credentials.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Treat TBAC as a local governance pattern; keep broad vendor and standard background upstream.

qualifying_findings.source_title: PERFOPT-Bench: Evaluating Coding Agents on Software Performance Optimization
qualifying_findings.visible_date: Showing new listings for Friday, 10 July 2026
qualifying_findings.summary: A new arXiv cs.SE listing introduced PERFOPT-Bench, which evaluates coding agents on performance optimization tasks using hidden correctness tests, verified speedup measurement, and trajectory-level audit.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Software engineering evals for agents should measure more than patch correctness. Performance optimization requires profiling, correctness preservation, reproducibility checks, and trajectory audit to prevent benchmark shortcut exploitation.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep local coverage to evaluation design and acceptance gates; broad benchmark cataloging belongs upstream.

qualifying_findings.source_title: DeepSWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Original, Long-Horizon Engineering Tasks
qualifying_findings.visible_date: Showing new listings for Friday, 10 July 2026
qualifying_findings.summary: The arXiv cs.SE new listing describes DeepSWE as a benchmark of 113 original long-horizon software engineering tasks for evaluating coding agents.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Agent evaluation should include original, long-horizon tasks that exercise planning, multi-file change management, and sustained verification rather than relying only on short issue-level fixes.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Use as downstream eval-practice evidence; route benchmark/entity background upstream.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Understanding Code Review in the Age of AI Coding Agents: An Interpretive Theory
qualifying_findings.visible_date: Showing new listings for Friday, 10 July 2026
qualifying_findings.summary: A July 10 arXiv cs.SE listing notes that coding agents now author entire pull requests and that practitioners disagree about whether code review becomes a bottleneck, remains necessary, or erodes engineering understanding.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Local code-review guidance should treat AI-authored PR review as an operating-model problem: review capacity, understanding retention, explicit reviewer responsibilities, and machine-assisted checks all need to be designed together.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep local synthesis on review workflow and team learning implications rather than a broad research-paper entity page.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Compiling Large Multi-Modal Requirement Documents into Runnable Software Systems: From an Agentic Test-Driven Perspective
qualifying_findings.visible_date: Showing new listings for Friday, 10 July 2026
qualifying_findings.summary: A replaced arXiv listing describes ARC, an agentic requirement compilation framework that turns DSL-based multi-modal requirement documents into runnable systems while generating architecture, tests, and traceability.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Requirements-to-code workflows should preserve traceability from requirements through design, tests, and implementation. The local TDD and request-package pages should track this as evidence for bidirectional test-driven agentic workflows.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Use locally for workflow traceability and agentic TDD practice; broad framework or benchmark background routes upstream.

qualifying_findings.source_title: TrajAudit: Automated Failure Diagnosis for Agentic Coding Systems
qualifying_findings.visible_date: Showing new listings for Friday, 10 July 2026
qualifying_findings.summary: A replaced arXiv listing describes TrajAudit, an automated failure diagnosis framework for repository-level coding-agent trajectories that folds low-signal context and uses test failure reports to focus investigation.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Agent traces need to be structured for diagnosis, not just retained. Local harness guidance should cover saliency reduction, test-failure priors, on-demand trace inspection, and earliest-error localization as evaluation and debugging patterns.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep local coverage to trace design and failure-diagnosis practice; route benchmark cataloging upstream.

qualifying_findings.summary: The public GitHub repository for Awesome Harness Engineering had a July 10 commit adding Shopify Roast to the task runners and orchestration section. qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: The commit is small, but the maintained resource list is a signal that harness engineering is consolidating around reusable categories: planning, context, permissions, memory, orchestration, verification, observability, and sandboxing.
